newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Aberdeen buy creates critical mass.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Aberdeen buy creates critical mass.

text.p: Aberdeen Asset Management said on Thursday its purchase of Scottish Provident's (SPI) Prolific Financial Management should give it the critical mass needed to compete in the investment management business.
"We are very comfortable. It takes us up to being a pretty significant player and we'll be the second biggest non-life fund manager in Scotland," Aberdeen chief executive Martin Gilbert told Reuters.
"We would clearly like to be 100 billion (sterling) but it'll take us a bit of time to get there," he said.
Aberdeen will pay 55.5 million sterling for Prolific through the issue of shares which will see SPI take a 41 percent stake in Aberdeen.
Funds under management at Aberdeen will jump to 11 billion sterling from the current 3.1 billion as a result.

SPI bought Prolific from Danish insurer Hafnia about four years ago for 61 million sterling net of cash, but SPI group managing director David Woods said it had effectively paid nothing for the asset management business.
He said the embedded value of the UK life business at the time was about 59 million and the offshore life business about two million. Both of these would be retained in SPI.
"As a rule of thumb we generally reckon we paid nothing for the asset managers," said Woods. "We are very pleased."
"If you go back, asset management companies were not trading for very much at all, it sort of came with the insurance companies at the time," said Woods.
He said SPI had worked hard to develop Prolific's external asset management business, which is where it had been able to "crystallise value".
Gilbert said it was too early to put a value on any cost savings, but due to the complementary nature of the businesses they were unlikely to be significant.

"Aberdeen's strengths in Asia, emerging markets, smaller companies, fixed interest and investment trusts are well matched by Prolific's track record in the UK equity income and technology sectors, unit trusts and offshore funds."
He said the deal was likely to be earnings-enhancing in the first full year on both the pre-tax and per-share level before any exceptional items.
Gilbert said it was likely to be Aberdeen's last acquisition for the moment as it digested the purchase, although if something came up in the interim he would look at it.
He said the deal made Aberdeen a significant player, placing it in the top 15 in the UK unit trust league.
"That is going to give us a lot of scope in that area. and we certainly see that growing," Gilbert said.
Aberdeen would also look to be bigger in the institutional pension fund business, with assets in that sector currently around 350 million sterling for the combined operation.
Of the 11 billion sterling under management about seven billion is for SPI. Woods said this was a high proportion and he would like to it reduced significantly over the coming years.
The combined operations of Aberdeen and Prolific will be named Aberdeen Prolific Asset Management Ltd.
Aberdeen investment trusts will retain their branding with UK-based unit trusts renamed Aberdeen Prolific.
SPI will be entitled to two seats on the board and representation on certain board committees.
Woods said the Aberdeen stake was regarded as a long term investment. "We plan to be in there for the long term."
